text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy's main opposition Freedom Alliance led in mayoral races in the key cities of Milan and Turin after a first round of voting on Sunday ended the separatist Northern League's control of the country's business capital (all).

* Hard left opposition leader Fausto Bertinotti warned the Democratic Party of the Left against contesting a second electoral round run-off on May 11 without their backing, saying the Olive Tree coalition was bound to collapse if it did not ally with them (all)

* The Group of Seven industrial nations met during the weekend in Washington. Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told reporters the G7 expressed appreciation for Italy's progress in reducing the budget deficit, its success in getting inflation down and its solid economy, but noted the slow pace of the country's recovery. At a news conference following the G7 meeting, Ciampi added he would not view negatively a reform of Value Added Tax, in line with other European Union directives, as inflation would not suffer. Bank of Italy's governor Antonio Fazio, however, disagreed with this view.

* Ciampi told the G7 meeting Italy was already working on the 1998 budget, as for the actual size of the deficit-cutting measures, seen up to 25 trillion lire, the minister said it was too early to speculate (La Stampa).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
